front: What does "modular RAG" mean as an architectural idea?
back: Treat indexing, pre-retrieval, routing, retrieval, post-retrieval, and generation as independent, swappable modules that different queries can move through differently, instead of every query taking one fixed retrieve-then-generate path.

front: What three routing mechanisms does this page compare for the same task?
back: Heuristic routing (keyword/pattern rules, no model call), embedding-based semantic routing (one local embedding call, no LLM), and LLM-based routing (the router reused from adaptive-rag/).

front: What 5 categories do all three routers classify a query into?
back: CLEAR, VAGUE, COMPOUND, BROAD, NEEDS_CONTEXT — the same categories Adaptive RAG's router uses to pick a pre-retrieval technique.

front: Why does this page evaluate routers on two separate test sets instead of one?
back: A router's accuracy on the queries used to design it (the "design set") can't distinguish real generalization from rules simply fit to those examples; a genuinely held-out set written without looking at the rules is needed to measure real-world accuracy.

front: What happened to the heuristic router's accuracy between the design set and the held-out set?
back: It collapsed from 1.00 (design set) to 0.40 (held-out) — measured brittleness, not a hypothetical caveat about keyword rules.

front: What were the embedding router's design-set and held-out accuracies, and why is that number called "more trustworthy"?
back: 0.67 on design set, 0.80 on held-out — roughly consistent across both, because its example utterances were never fit to either set.

front: What's the accuracy/latency/cost trade-off of the LLM router versus the other two?
back: 1.00 accuracy on both test sets (the only router both accurate and consistent everywhere), but ~1500ms average latency versus ~0ms (heuristic) and ~50ms (embedding), plus a real per-call API cost the other two don't have.

front: How do Self-RAG, Corrective RAG, and Agentic RAG relate to modular RAG?
back: All are modular RAG instances differing only in what decides which module runs: Self-RAG and CRAG bake a self-evaluation/correction loop into the orchestration module, while Agentic RAG has an LLM make that routing/looping decision itself at runtime.
